<p><img src="/assets/img/rope-to-yarn/14-pi-lowers-every-slope.png" alt="PI lowers every slope, including the fast one: side-by-side diagrams compare original RoPE with position interpolation at scale four."></p>
<h2>12. YaRN Changes Frequencies Selectively</h2>
<h3>What This Section Wants to Say</h3>
<p>Now we arrive at <strong>YaRN</strong>! Look at the dilemma we just uncovered:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Original RoPE</strong> is great for <strong>Pair 0</strong> (keeps neighboring words <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mtext> rad</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\text{ rad}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord"> rad</span></span></span></span></span> apart), but breaks on <strong>Pair 3</strong> at position <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3500</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">3500</span></span></span></span>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Position Interpolation (PI)</strong> fixes <strong>Pair 3</strong> at position <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3500</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">3500</span></span></span></span>, but ruins <strong>Pair 0</strong>'s sharp spacing for neighboring words.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p>YaRN's frequency rule—called <strong>NTK-by-parts</strong>—asks a brilliant question: <strong>"Why not do BOTH?"</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>If a clock hand spun <strong>32 full circles or more</strong> during training (<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>fast</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{\text{fast}} = 32</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8889em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0528em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3361em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0528em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">fast</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">32</span></span></span></span>), <strong>keep its original fast speed (</strong><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">100%</span></span></span></span><strong>)</strong>!</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>If a clock hand spun <strong>1 full circle or less</strong> during training (<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mtext>slow</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{\text{slow}} = 1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8889em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0528em;">β</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3361em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0528em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">slow</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span>), <strong>slow it down by</strong> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s=4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">s</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span> <strong>just like PI</strong>!</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>If a clock hand is <strong>in between 1 and 32 circles</strong>, <strong>blend the two speeds smoothly</strong> using a slider weight <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_i</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.625em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0556em;">γ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0556em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>!</p>
</li>
</ul>

The two uses of the word "interpolation" are related but distinct!)</em></p>
<h3>Crucial Research Detail: Paper Ramp vs. Code Ramp</h3>
<p>If you compare the YaRN paper (Section 3.2) with the official Hugging Face <code>transformers</code> implementation, they compute the middle slider weights <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_i</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.625em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0556em;">γ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3117em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0556em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight">i</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> in two slightly different ways:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>The Paper's Ramp (Linear in Rotation Count</strong> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">r</span></span></span></span><strong>):</strong></li>
</ol>
<span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>γ</mi><mtext>paper</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">clip</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo separator="true">,</mo><mtext>  </mtext><mn>0</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mtext>  </mtext><mn>1</mn><mo fence="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma_{\text{paper}}(r) = \operatorname{clip}\left(\frac{r - 1}{32 - 1}, \; 0, \; 1\right)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.0361em;vertical-align:-0.2861em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" <h3>The Step-by-Step Breakdown</h3>
<p>Start with the training-turn formula from Section 7 and solve it step-by-step for the pair index <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6595em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">i</span></span></span></span>:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Start with turns</strong> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">r</span></span></span></span><strong>:</strong></li>

<p>The rounded implementation rounds the lower boundary <strong>down</strong> (floor <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌊</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">⌋</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lfloor \cdot \rfloor</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">⌊</span><span class="mord">⋅</span><span class="mclose">⌋</span></span></span></span>) and the upper boundary <strong>up</strong> (ceiling <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌈</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">⌉</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lceil \cdot \rceil</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">⌈</span><span class="mord">⋅</span><span class="mclose">⌉</span></span></span></span>) to lock onto integer pair indices:</p>

<p><em>(Remember: large angles like</em> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3500</mn><mtext> radians</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3500\text{ radians}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">3500</span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord"> radians</span></span></span></span></span> <em>are completely valid—sine and cosine wrap around every</em> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">2</span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0359em;">π</span></span></span></span> <em>radians automatically).</em></p>

We got the best of both worlds!</p>

<h2>15. Does YaRN Remove the Shortcut?</h2>
<h3>What This Section Wants to Say</h3>
<p>Remember the "positional odometer shortcut" <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">S</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span> from Section 9, where the AI used the dot product with Token 0 to guess how far into the document it was?</p>
<p>Does YaRN erase that shortcut? <strong>No—it stretches (compresses) it so it doesn't wrap around and break!</strong> Under YaRN, Position <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3500</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">3500</span></span></span></span> produces the exact same <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>0.7675</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(p) \approx +0.7675</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">S</span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">+</span><span class="mord">0.7675</span></span></span></span> signal that Position <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>875</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">875</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">875</span></span></span></span> used to produce during training.</p>

<p>That is the exact same value that ordinary RoPE produced at position <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>875</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">875</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">875</span></span></span></span>:</p>

<p><em>(Note: Row</em> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3996</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3996</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">3996</span></span></span></span> <em>shows the exact coordinate match with old position</em> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>999</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">999</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">999</span></span></span></span><em>; the actual final token of a 4,000-token sequence is</em> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3999</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3999</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">3999</span></span></span></span><em>).</em></p>
<p><strong>Two Honest Limitations to Keep in Mind:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Compressing a cue</strong> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo mathvariant="normal">≠</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\neq</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8889em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mrel"><span class="mrel"><span class="mord vbox"><span class="thinbox"><span class="rlap"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8889em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="inner"><span class="mord"><span class="mrel"></span></span></span><span class="fix"></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace nobreak"></span><span class="mrel">=</span></span></span></span></span> <strong>erasing a shortcut:</strong> Because <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Y</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\mathrm{YaRN}}(p)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0576em;">S</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3283em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0576em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mathrm mtight">YaRN</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mopen">(</span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mclose">)</span></span></span></span> still climbs smoothly from <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span> to <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.841</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.841</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.841</span></span></span></span> across the 4,000-token window, YaRN prevents the signal from flipping negative at <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3500</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">3500</span></span></span></span>, but it does not magically erase a model's reliance on position cues.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Static vs. Dynamic Scaling:</strong> With our fixed <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s = 4</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">s</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">4</span></span></span></span>, this slower speed (<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.00025</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.00025</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.00025</span></span></span></span>) is active <em>even if you only feed the model a short 500-word prompt</em>! Fixed YaRN does not know in advance whether your document will be <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">500</span></span></span></span> tokens or <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4,000</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8389em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord">4</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">000</span></span></span></span> tokens long (adjusting <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">s</span></span></span></span> on the fly based on current sequence length is a separate option called <em>Dynamic Scaling</em>).</p>
</li>
</ol>
<h2>16. Why Attention Also Needs a Strength Adjustment</h2>
<h3>What This Section Wants to Say</h3>
<p>Up to this point, we have fixed the <strong>angles</strong> of the arrows. Why does Full YaRN also need a <strong>second</strong> step that stretches the <strong>length</strong> of the arrows?</p>
<p>Because of <strong>Attention Dilution (The Crowd Noise Problem)</strong>! After the AI computes raw dot-product scores (logits), it passes them through <strong>Softmax</strong>, which acts like a raffle where every word gets positive tickets (<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>z</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^z</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6644em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">e</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.6644em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mathnormal mtight" style="margin-right:0.044em;">z</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>) and all percentages must add up to <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">100%</span></span></span></span>. Even a completely irrelevant background word ("distractor") with a score of <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z = 0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.044em;">z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span> still gets <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^0 = 1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8141em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">e</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">0</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span></span></span></span> <strong>free raffle ticket</strong>!</p>
<p>When you jump from <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1,000</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8389em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">000</span></span></span></span> words to <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4,000</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8389em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord">4</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">000</span></span></span></span> words, adding <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo class="mord">000</span></span></span></span> extra distractor tickets into the raffle bucket waters down a strong matching word's attention share from <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>12.93</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12.93\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">12.93%</span></span></span></span> <strong>down to</strong> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.58</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.58\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">3.58%</span></span></span></span>!</p>

<p>Here, <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>2.71828</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e \approx 2.71828</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4831em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">e</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">2.71828</span></span></span></span>. Raising <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">e</span></span></span></span> to each score makes every weight strictly positive, and dividing by the sum forces all allowed weights to add up to <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">1.0</span></span></span></span> (<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">100%</span></span></span></span>).</p>
<h3>A Controlled Raffle Competition: 1,000 vs. 4,000 Tokens</h3>
<p>To isolate the effect of adding more competing keys, let's run a clean test:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Suppose <strong>1 relevant target key</strong> has a strong match logit of <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z = 5</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.044em;">z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">5</span></span></span></span>, which gives it <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>≈</mo><mn>148.413159</mn><mtext> tickets</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^5 \approx 148.413159\text{ tickets}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8141em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">e</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">5</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">148.413159</span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord"> tickets</span></span></span></span></span>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Every other allowed key is an irrelevant <strong>distractor</strong> with a logit of <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z = 0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.044em;">z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span>, which still gets <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mtext> ticket each</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^0 = 1\text{ ticket each}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8141em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">e</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">0</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord"> ticket each</span></span></span></span></span>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><em>(Note: These logits</em> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">5</span></span></span></span> <em>and</em> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span> <em>are clean illustrative assumptions, not derived from our</em> <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1..8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1..8]</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord">1..8</span><span class="mclose">]</span></span></span></span> <em>query. </li>

<p>With <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6833em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.109em;">N</span></span></span></span> distractors, the relevant key's share of the raffle bucket is:</p>
<span class="katex-display"><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><menclose notation="box"><mstyle <h2>17. Calculate YaRN's Attention-Strength Factor</h2>
<h3>What This Section Wants to Say</h3>
<p>To rescue that diluted <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.58</mn><mi style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">12.93%</span></span></span></span>, YaRN makes the winning matches "speak louder" by stretching the length of every rotated Query and Key arrow by a factor <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.1386</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">13.86\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">13.86%</span></span></span></span> longer).</p>
<p>Because <strong>both</strong> the Query and the Key are multiplied by <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" encoding="application/x-tex">29.65\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" That boosts our target word's logit from <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation As a result, the relevant word's attention share recovers to <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>14.05</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14.05\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">14.05%</span></span></span></span>!</p>
<h3>The Step-by-Step Breakdown</h3>
<p>For LLaMA-family models, the YaRN paper recommends this arrow-scaling formula (fitted empirically by testing on real models):</p>

<p>Here, <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation <td><strong>4,000 allowed keys</strong>, logits multiplied by <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c^2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8141em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> (<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>6.48</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z \approx 6.48</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4831em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.044em;">z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">6.48</span></span></span></span>)</td>
<td><span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>14.0467</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14.0467\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">14.0467%</span></span></span></span> <em>(Recovered!)</em></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p><strong>Three Essential Rules About Temperature Scaling:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Why multiply instead of adding a constant?</strong> If you added <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.48</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.48</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">+</span><span class="mord">1.48</span></span></span></span> to <em>every</em> score, the distractors would also go up from <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0</span></span></span></span> to <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1.48</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+1.48</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">+</span><span class="mord">1.48</span></span></span></span>, multiplying everyone's tickets by <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>1.48</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{1.48}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8141em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">e</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1.48</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>—which cancels out in the fraction and leaves Softmax <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>100</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">100%</span></span></span></span> unchanged! Multiplication stretches the <strong>gap</strong> between high scores and low scores.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Temperature scaling cannot fix bad angles:</strong> Multiplying by <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c^2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8141em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> only makes the current 1st-place score win by a bigger margin. If the wrong key had the highest score (because you didn't fix the frequencies first), multiplying by <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c^2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8141em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> would just make the model <em>more confident in its mistake</em>!</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Empirical tuning:</strong> Landing at <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>14.05</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14.05\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">14.05%</span></span></span></span> vs. <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>12.93</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12.93\%</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8056em;vertical-align:-0.0556em;"></span><span class="mord">12.93%</span></span></span></span> depends on our chosen <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=5</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.044em;">z</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">5</span></span></span></span> example; <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 1 + 0.1\ln s</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">0.1</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mop">ln</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">s</span></span></span></span> is a general empirical rule, not an exact algebraic inverse for every distribution.</p>
</li>
</ol>

class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2861em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>
<p>Since we haven't invented vectors for the other <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3,500</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8389em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord">3</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">500</span></span></span></span> words in the book, we leave those final sums symbolic rather than making up a fake percentage!</p>
<h3>Summary of Our Complete 9-Step Path</h3>
<ol>
<li>
<p>Start with the eight query coordinates <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.625em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0359em;">q</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">2</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">3</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">4</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">5</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">6</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">7</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">8</span><span class="mclose">]</span></span></span></span>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Calculate the four original RoPE speeds <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0.01</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0.001</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = [1, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001]</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.1</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.01</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.001</span><span class="mclose">]</span></span></span></span>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Use training-window rotation counts to compute YaRN's blended speeds <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo mathvariant="normal" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0.075</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0.005</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0.00025</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta' = [1, 0.075, 0.005, 0.00025]</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7519em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">θ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.7519em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord mtight">′</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.075</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.005</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.00025</span><span class="mclose">]</span></span></span></span>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Multiply the adjusted speeds by the token position <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p = 3500</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.625em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">3500</span></span></span></span> to get angles <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>3500</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>262.5</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>17.5</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>0.875</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[3500, 262.5, 17.5, 0.875]</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1em;vertical-align:-0.25em;"></span><span class="mopen">[</span><span class="mord">3500</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">262.5</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">17.5</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">0.875</span><span class="mclose">]</span></span></span></span>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Rotate each 2D coordinate pair using <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mop">cos</span></span></span></span> and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6679em;"></span><span class="mop">sin</span></span></span></span>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Stretch the rotated Query and Key vectors by <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.138629</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 1 + 0.1\ln s \approx 1.138629</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">1</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span><span class="mbin">+</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2222em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">0.1</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mop">ln</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">s</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">≈</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">1.138629</span></span></span></span>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Compute the dot product and divide by <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mi>D</mi></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>8</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{D} = \sqrt{8}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:1.04em;vertical-align:-0.1133em;"></span><span class="mord sqrt"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.9267em;"><span class="svg-align" style="top:-3em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="mord" style="padding-left:0.833em;"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em;">D</span></span></span><span style="top:-2.8867em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:3em;"></span><span class="hide-tail" style="min-width:0.853em;height:1.08em;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="400em" height="1.08em" viewBox="0 0 400000 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin slice"><path d="M95,702

<h2>19. Why Fine-Tuning and Evaluation Still Matter</h2>
<h3>What This Section Wants to Say</h3>
<p>YaRN is an incredible mathematical bridge—in fact, it often lets models read longer prompts with <em>zero</em> extra training, or with <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\times</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7278em;vertical-align:-0.0833em;"></span><span class="mord">10</span><span class="mord">×</span></span></span></span> fewer fine-tuning steps than Position Interpolation.</p>
<p>However, YaRN is <strong>not magic pixie dust</strong>. Even after YaRN fixes the clock speeds and boosts the attention strength, a short fine-tuning run on long texts is still hugely beneficial. Why? Because inside the AI's brain, changing the middle clock speeds changes how the 4 pairs add together!</p>
<h3>The Five Reasons Fine-Tuning Still Helps</h3>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Fast and slow frequencies now combine differently:</strong> Remember that the total dot product adds <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>Pair</mtext><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mtext>Pair</mtext><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mtext>Pair</mtext><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mtext>Pair</mtext><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Pair}_0 + \text{Pair}_1 + \text{Pair}_2 + \text{Pair}_3</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8333em;vertical-align:-0.15em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord text"><span class="mord">Pair</span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">0</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" class="mord">Pair</span></span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3011em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3011em;"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em;"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span>. During training, when Pair 3 was at <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.875</mn><mtext> rad</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.875\text{ rad}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">0.875</span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord"> rad</span></span></span></span></span> (which used to happen at token <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>875</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">875</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">875</span></span></span></span>), Pair 0 was at <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>875</mn><mtext> rad</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">875\text{ rad}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">875</span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord"> rad</span></span></span></span></span>. The cross-frequency combinations are new.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Intermediate frequencies still extrapolate:</strong> Pairs 1 and 2 were only partially slowed down (<span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.075</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.075</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.075</span></span></span></span> and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.005</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.005</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">0.005</span></span></span></span>), so at <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=3500</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.625em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">p</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span><span class="mrel">=</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.2778em;"></span></span><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">3500</span></span></span></span> they reach <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>262.5</mn><mtext> rad</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">262.5\text{ rad}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">262.5</span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord"> rad</span></span></span></span></span> and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>17.5</mn><mtext> rad</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17.5\text{ rad}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">17.5</span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord"> rad</span></span></span></span></span>—beyond their training maximums of <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.9</mn><mtext> rad</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99.9\text{ rad}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">99.9</span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord"> rad</span></span></span></span></span> and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>9.99</mn><mtext> rad</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.99\text{ rad}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6944em;"></span><span class="mord">9.99</span><span class="mord text"><span class="mord"> rad</span></span></span></span></span>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>More keys compete in Softmax:</strong> Our <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c^2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8141em;"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">c</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.8141em;"><span style="top:-3.063em;margin-right:0.05em;"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em;"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> boost helps counter dilution on average, but real attention distributions vary wildly across heads and layers.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Information is separated by unfamiliar semantic distances:</strong> Even if the clock angles are familiar, tracking a pronoun across <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo separator="true">,</mo><mn>500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3,500</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8389em;vertical-align:-0.1944em;"></span><span class="mord">3</span><span class="mpunct">,</span><span class="mspace" style="margin-right:0.1667em;"></span><span class="mord">500</span></span></span></span> words of story plot is harder than tracking it across <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mn>500</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">500</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6444em;"></span><span class="mord">500</span></span></span></span> words.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Learned shortcuts may persist:</strong> As we saw in Section 15, rescaling compresses position cues rather than deleting them.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<p><em>(Also remember: calling fast pairs "local" and slow pairs "global" is a helpful intuition about how fast their angles change with distance, not a strict law banning fast pairs from helping with long-range retrieval or slow pairs from carrying local meaning!)</em></p>

<h2>Appendix A. Small Reproducible Python Example</h2>
<p>This script uses <strong>only Python's built-in <code>math</code> library</strong> (zero external dependencies). Run it to verify every single number, vector, and assertion in this blog post!</p>
<pre><code>import math

D = 8
BASE = 10_000.0
TRAIN_LENGTH = 1_000
NEW_LENGTH = 4_000
SCALE = NEW_LENGTH / TRAIN_LENGTH
QUERY = [1., 2., 3., 4., 5., 6., 7., 8.]
FIRST_KEY = [0., 0., 0., 0., 0., 0., -8., 7.]

def clip01(value):
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, value))

theta = [BASE ** (-2 * i / D) for i in range(D // 2)]

def correction_index(turns):
    return (
        D * math.log(TRAIN_LENGTH / (2 * math.pi * turns))
        / (2 * math.log(BASE))
    )

# For this example the rounded endpoints are 0 and 3.
low = math.floor(correction_index(32))
high = math.ceil(correction_index(1))
assert (low, high) == (0, 3)

gamma = [
    1 - clip01((i - low) / (high - low))
    for i in range(D // 2)
]
theta_pi = [frequency / SCALE for frequency in theta]
theta_yarn = [
    (1 - weight) * frequency / SCALE + weight * frequency
    for frequency, weight in zip(theta, gamma)
]

def rotate(vector, position, frequencies):
    assert len(vector) == 2 * len(frequencies)
    output = []
    for i, frequency in enumerate(frequencies):
        x, y = vector[2 * i : 2 * i + 2]
        angle = position * frequency
        cosine, sine = math.cos(angle), math.sin(angle)
        output.extend([
            x * cosine - y * sine,
            x * sine + y * cosine,
        ])
    return output

def dot(a, b):
    return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))

def display(values):
    return [round(value, 6) for value in values]

print("Original speeds:", theta)
print("PI speeds:", theta_pi)
print("Preservation weights:", gamma)
print("YaRN speeds:", theta_yarn)

for name, frequencies in [
    ("RoPE", theta),
    ("PI", theta_pi),
    ("YaRN rotations", theta_yarn),
]:
    for position in [2, 3500]:
        result = rotate(QUERY, position, frequencies)
        print(name, position, display(result))
        # Pure rotations preserve the vector's squared length.
        assert math.isclose(dot(result, result), 204.0, rel_tol=1e-12)

c = 1 + 0.1 * math.log(SCALE)
q_rotated = rotate(QUERY, 3500, theta_yarn)
k_rotated = rotate(FIRST_KEY, 0, theta_yarn)
q_scaled = [c * value for value in q_rotated]
k_scaled = [c * value for value in k_rotated]

logit_before = dot(q_rotated, k_rotated) / math.sqrt(D)
logit_after = dot(q_scaled, k_scaled) / math.sqrt(D)

assert math.isclose(
    logit_after, c * c * logit_before, rel_tol=1e-12
)
assert math.isclose(
    dot(q_rotated, k_rotated) / 113,
    math.sin(0.875),
    rel_tol=1e-12,
)
print("Full YaRN query:", display(q_scaled))
print("c:", c, "logit multiplier:", c * c)
print("Exact toy key logit before/after:", logit_before, logit_after)

# Separate controlled competition experiment.
# Logit 5 is an illustrative assumption, not the toy query's logit.
def relevant_weight(logit, distractor_count):
    # Algebraically equivalent to exp(logit)/(exp(logit)+N),
    # with zero logits for all distractors.
    return 1 / (1 + distractor_count * math.exp(-logit))

print("1000 keys:", relevant_weight(5, 999))
print("4000 keys:", relevant_weight(5, 3999))
print("4000 keys, scaled:", relevant_weight(5 * c * c, 3999))

</code></pre>
<h2>Sources and Scope</h2>
<p>The numerical examples and diagrams in this guide are worked educational examples designed to make the underlying mathematics concrete; they are not measurements from a specific trained model.</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p><strong>Su et al. (2021)</strong>, <em>RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding</em> — RoPE's formulation and relative-position dot-product identity.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Chen et al. (2023)</strong>, <em>Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Positional Interpolation</em> — Position Interpolation (PI) and context-extension fine-tuning experiments.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Peng et al. (2023)</strong>, <em>YaRN: Efficient Context Window Extension of Large Language Models</em> — Sections 3.2 and 3.3 cover NTK-by-parts frequency blending and attention temperature scaling.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>YaRN Authors' Repository</strong> (<code>jquesnelle/yarn</code>) — Reference implementations and released long-context models.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Hugging Face <code>transformers</code> RoPE Utilities</strong> — Code reference for the rounded pair-index ramp (<code>low</code> / <code>high</code> floor and ceiling endpoints) used throughout this walkthrough.</p>
</li>
</ol>
